Using rockyIntertidal R pkg.

Using the rockyIntertidal R package

Getting started

Installation

Step 1. Install R, RStudio, and RTools in Company Portal

Install R 4.5 or higher, RStudio, and Rtools45 (DOI-DO-RTools 4.5.6608 on Company Portal) from Company Portal. Note that R and RTools versions generally need to match. However, according to CRAN Rtools45 works for R 4.6 and the yet to be released R 4.7.

Step 2. Install pak package in R: 

install.packages('pak')

Step 3. Install rockyIntertidal from GitHub

Note that whenever the rockyIntertidal package is updated, you can rerun this code to install the latest version.

library(pak)
pkg_install("doi-nps/rockyIntertidal")

Step 4. Load rockyIntertidal R package 

library(rockyIntertidal)

Step 5. Import rocky monitoring data

Note that R is not able to connect to files on Sharepoint or MS Teams (b/c Teams also stores all files on Sharepoint). That means you need to store data package files on your local machine or on a server (e.g. NETN Z drive). The default option for importing data will add the data package views (i.e., flatfiles) to an environment called ROCKY to your Environment work space (i.e. Environment tab in top right panel). If you would rather import each individual view into your R session, specify with the new_env argument (e.g., importData(new_env = F)). To import data using the default settings (i.e. run importData() with no arguments), you must have the rocky intertidal data package front end set as a User DSN called rocky_FE. The database front end must also be linked with the latest rocky intertidal backend to pull in the latest data (see “Setting up DSN” tab for more details).

Option 1. Import data via .csv files. The file path should be where csvs are on your machine or server. 

importData(type = 'csv',
           filepath = "../data/rocky") # update filepath to your computer

Option 2. Import data via zip file of csvs. The filepath should be the location and name of the zip file. 

importData(type = 'zip',
           filepath = "../data/rocky/NETN_RockyIntertidal_Data_Package_20260917.zip")

Option 3. Import data via data package database file on your computer 

importData(type = 'dbfile',
           filepath = "../data/rocky/NETN_RockyIntertidal_FE_DataPackage_20241211.accdb")

Option 4. Import data via data package database DSN (Data Source Name) on your computer. Note that this is the default setting. As long as you have a named DSN called “rocky_FE” that links to the data package FE database, and that database links to the latest rocky intertidal backend database, the code below will run. See Setting up DSN tab for how to set up DSN. 

importData() # easiest
importData(type = 'DSN', odbc = "rocky_FE") # equivalent to line above

Step 6. (Optional) Export data package to zip

You can export all of the csvs to a zip file with the day’s date stamped on the file name. This allows you to import the tables from the database, then export the csvs as one zip file.

exportData(filepath = "./data", zip = TRUE) 
exportData(filepath = "../data", zip = FALSE)

Step 6b.Import water temperature data NOTE: NOT RECENTLY TESTED/NOT CURRENTLY ACTIVE

The water temperature data is stored as separate csvs and so has a different import function and process. The temp logger files will go into your ROCKY environment named the 6 letter location code. The buoy = T loads the buoy data for each park to the ROCKY environment. The simplify = T simplifies the datasets to include only 1 logger measurement per high tide event (for water temp) and 1 buoy record per day. All plotting functions require the simplified data. The latest compiled files are on the Z drive here: “../Rocky_Intertidal/NETN/5_Data/Data_Files/Temperature/Compiled_HT_water_temps_2011-2022/”.

path = "../data/rocky/temp_data/Compiled_HT_water_temps"
importWaterTemp(path = path, buoy = T, simplify = T)

Step 7. Play with the data

The functions in the rockyIntertidal package are designed to work with the views, and are the best way to interact with the data to query by park, site, site type, year, parameter, etc. However, if you want to view the raw data, and you imported the data into the ROCKY environment, you can access them with the code below:

# See list of the views
names(ROCKY)

# View one of the views
View(ROCKY$Bolts)

# See top 6 records 
head(ROCKY$Echinoderm_Counts)

# Check structure of view
str(ROCKY$Echinoderm_Counts)

# Assign a view to a data frame named bolts in R. Interact with bolts the way you would work with any normal data frame in R. 
bolts <- ROCKY$Bolts


While the above code works, the better approach is to use the “get”, “sum” or “plot” functions within the R package, which access the same files, but allow you to also query, summarize, and plot data based on park, location, years, plot name, species, etc. The functions in this package also drop QAQC visits and other duplicates (e.g. barnacle counts) in the data by default, making analysis easier and more repeatable.

Package Design

The package has 4 main types of functions to facilitate working with rocky interidal data:
  • import/export: facilitates importing and exporting data package views in R.
  • get: Each view in the data package has a get function that allows you to query by park, site, year, community, species, etc. In general, the get functions return raw data from the views.
  • sum: Most views in the data package also have a summary function that allows you to summarize plot-level data, such as average cover of species by photoplot community type. The get file for that view is used under the hood.
  • plot: most views also have a plotting function that typically uses the sum function under the hood and visualizes the data for that view. All plotting functions return a ggplot2 object, which means you can usually add ggplot geoms, scales, etc. to them (though note if a scale is already used under the hood, you may not be able to specify another).

Getting help

Getting (and improving) help

The functions in rockyIntertidal have help documentation like any R package. To view the help, you can go to the Packages tab and click on rockyIntertidal (see below). That will show you all the functions in the package. Clicking on individual functions will take you to the help documentation for that function.

You can also see the help of a function by running, for example: 

?importData

If rockyIntertidal isn’t loaded yet, you’d run: 

?rockyIntertidal::importData

Each function’s help includes a Description, Usage (i.e. function arguments and their defaults), Argument options/definitions, and several examples showing how the function can be used. This is where you come in! If you notice typos or can think of better descriptions, examples, error messages, etc., please send them my way! After we’re more comfortable with R packages and get versed on GitHub, you’ll be able to make those changes directly in the package. For now, you can just send me your suggestions and I’ll make the changes.

Finally, if you ever want to peak under the hood at the function, you can view it several ways.
  1. Keep F2 key pressed and click on the function name in R. This trick works for many but not all functions in R.

  2. View code in the GitHub doi-nps/rockyIntertidal repo. The functions are in the R folder.

Setting up DSN

Setting up a DSN

  1. Go to Windows Start Menu and search ODBC. Click on ODBC Data Sources (64-bit)
  2. Click on Add, then select Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb) then click Finish in next menu.

  3. Enter rocky_BE into the Data Source Name (red arrow), click on Select (red circle). In new window, click on C:/ (orange arrow) and find the path to your database. If it’s on the Z drive, then click on the Drives window and select correct Drive. Click on the data package database (yellow arrow). When complete, click OK. Finally, add the name of the database file to the Description (blue arrow), so it’s easier to check whether you’re using the latest version.

  4. If updating an existing DSN, follow similar process, except click on the DSN in the first window and select Configure instead of Add.

get Data functions

getBolts()

This function filters bolt data by park, site, plot type or plot name. Bolts are location-level and do not contain visit data.

Default, returns all records except blank X/Y or elevations 

bolts <- getBolts()

getEvents()

This function filters events and returns notes recorded during sampling events by park, site, plot name, and species. All visit-level get functions include this function under the hood to filter on park, site, year, etc.

Return all non-QAQC events (default)

getEchinoCounts()

This function filters echinoderm count data by park, site, and plot name. If a given species was not detected during a visit, its count is 0. Species codes are: ASTFOR = Asterias forbesi (Northern sea star); ASTRUB = Asterias rubens (common sea star); HENSAN = Henricia sanguinolenta (blood sea star); STRDRO = Strongylocentrotus droebachiensis (sea urchin).

Default filter returns all records except QAQC visits and blank counts 

ech <- getEchinoCounts()
print_head(ech)

getMotileInvertCounts()

This function filters motile invertebrate count data by park, site, and plot name. The returned data frame lists counts of each species detected for each sampling event and plot. Species codes in the data set are: CARMAE = Carcinus maenas (green crab); HEMISAN = Hemigrapsus sanguineus (Asian shore crab); LITLIT = Littorina littorea (common periwinkle); LITOBT = Littorina obtusata (smooth periwinkle); LITSAX = Littorina saxatilis (rough periwinkle); NUCLAP = Nucella lapillus (dogwhelk), TECTES = Tectura testudinalis (limpet).

Default filter returns all records except QAQC visits and blank counts 

motinv <- getMotileInvertCounts()
print_head(motinv)

getMotileInvertMeas()

This function filters motile invertebrate measurement data by park, site, and plot name. The returned data frame lists measurement data of each species detected for each sampling event and plot. Species codes in the data set are: CARMAE = Carcinus maenas (green crab); HEMISAN = Hemigrapsus sanguineus (Asian shore crab); LITLIT = Littorina littorea (common periwinkle); LITOBT = Littorina obtusata (smooth periwinkle); LITSAX = Littorina saxatilis (rough periwinkle); NUCLAP = Nucella lapillus (dogwhelk); TECTES = Tectura testudinalis (limpet).

Default filter returns all records except QAQC visits and blank measurements 

minv <- getMotileInvertMeas()

Summary Functions

sumBarnacleRecruitment()

The barnacle recruitment summary function calculates the median, min and max of counts for a given plot type (ie summer or winter) for each visit. If there are multiple records for a given site x visit x plot type, you will receive a warning in the console with a description of how the duplicates were handled by the function.

Summarize defaults, which is all parks, all sites, all years, all species, summer-only, non-QAQC visits/QAQC types, and complete records. 

barn <- sumBarnacleRecruitment()

sumPISpecies()

This function relates bolt elevation data with point intercept species detection data by park, site, plot name, and species. Returned values include elevation change between bolts, median elevation between bolts, min/max elevation between bolts, distance between bolts, slope percent and degree between bolts, horizontal distance between bolts, and interpolated elevation for point intercept sampling sites. Note: you will get a warning if there are impossible distance/elevation combinations in the console and an object called bolt_checks will show up in your workspace environment.

Summarize defaults, which is all parks, all sites, all years, all species, non-QAQC visits, and complete records.

Plotting Functions

plotBarnacleRecruitment()

This function plots median barnacle recruitment counts across the five summer plots per site and year, with error bars representing min and max counts among the five plots. If only 1 plot is specified, then the raw counts will be plotted. If both summer and winter plots are specified, resulting plot will be color-coded by season. If more than one site and year is specified, results will be faceted by site. Note that you will receive a warning if there are duplicate count records for a given site, plot name, and visit.

Plot summer recruitment for all years faceted on ACAD sites 

plotBarnacleRecruitment(park = 'ACAD')

Plot summer and winter recruitment for all years faceted on ACAD sites 

barn <- plotBarnacleRecruitment(park = 'ACAD', plotName = "all")
barn

Plot summer recruitment faceted on BOHA sites for 2024 

boha <- plotBarnacleRecruitment(park = 'BOHA', years = 2024)
boha

Plot raw S5 recruitment for all years faceted on BOHA sites. Individual plots may be useful for QC. 

boha_s5 <- plotBarnacleRecruitment(park = 'BOHA', plotName = "S5")
boha_s5

plotBuoyData()

This function plots water temperature at high tide by site. Note that function works on compiled logger data, rather than working off the raw logger data. Compiled datasets should be imported using importWaterTemp(). To speed up plotting of multiple sites or long time-series, plot the simplified water temperature data derived from importWaterTemp(simplify = TRUE). NOTE: NOT CURRENTLY ACTIVE; CODE IN THIS SECTION WAS NOT RUN.

Default filter returns a plot with min/max daily water temperature and max daily windspeed in mph, and wind direction recorded for winds > 35 miles/hour for the closest buoys to ACAD and BOHA 

plotBuoyData()

Plot windspeed for BOHA for all years 

plotBuoyData(park = "BOHA", metric = "wspd")

Plot all metrics for 2020 in ACAD 

plotBuoyData(park = "ACAD", years = 2020)

plotEchinoCounts()

This function plots average counts by species for a given park, site, years and species. The point for each species is the median count across the tidepools for that site, year and species. The error bars are the middle 50% (lower 25% and upper 75% quantiles) recorded in tidepools for a species. Note that if more than 1 site is specified, the resulting figure will facet on those variables.

Plot echinoderm counts for Outer Brewster from 2013 to 2021 

outbrew <- plotEchinoCounts(site = "OUTBRE", years = 2013:2021)
outbrew

Plot echinoderm counts for BOHA sites with legend position set to bottom 

boha <- plotEchinoCounts(park = "BOHA") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
boha

Plot echinoderm counts for sea stars in ACAD, dropping X and changing Y axis labels 

stars <- plotEchinoCounts(park = "ACAD", species = c("ASTFOR", "ASTRUB"), xlab = NULL, ylab = "Asterias spp. mean counts")
stars

plotEchinoMeas()

This function plots a heatmap of the distribution of invertebrate size classes in 1 mm increments by year for each specified site, target species photoplot, and species.

Plot echinoderm measurements for all species in Ship Harbor from 2013 to 2019 

ship <- plotEchinoMeas(site = "SHIHAR", years = 2013:2019)
ship

Plot echinoderm measurements for Bass Harbor for sea urchin 

bas_str <- plotEchinoMeas(site = "BASHAR", species = "STRDRO")
bas_str

Plot echinoderm measurements of common sea star for BOHA sites 

boha_ast <- plotEchinoMeas(park = "BOHA", species = "ASTRUB")
boha_ast

plotMotileInvertCounts()

This function plots median count by species for a given park, site, years and target species. The point for each species is the median count across the photoplots that site, year and target species. The error bars are the middle 50% (lower 25% and upper 75% quantiles) recorded in photoplots for a target species. Note that if more than 1 site is specified, more than one target species is specified, or both, the resulting figure will facet on those variables.

Plot motile invertebrate counts for all species in Outer Brewster from 2013 to 2019 

outbre <- plotMotileInvertCounts(site = "OUTBRE", years = 2013:2021)
outbre

Plot motile invertebrate counts for all species in Little Hunter Barnacle photoplots 

lithun <- plotMotileInvertCounts(site = "LITHUN", community = "Barnacle")
lithun

Plot Littorina species counts in Little Hunter with legend position on right 

peri <- c("LITLIT", "LITOBT", "LITSAX")
lh_peri <- plotMotileInvertCounts(site = "LITHUN", species = peri) + theme(legend.position = 'right')
lh_peri

Plot dogwhelk counts Ship Harbor photoplots, dropping legend. 

ship_dog <- plotMotileInvertCounts(site = "SHIHAR", species = "NUCLAP") + theme(legend.position = "none")
ship_dog

plotMotileInvertMeas()

This function plots a heatmap of the distribution of invertebrate size classes in 1 mm increments by year for each specified site, target species photoplot, and species. To ensure facets are working properly, can either specify multiple sites or specify multiple communities, but not both. Not every combination of facet may be plotted correctly. If the returned plot has multiple numbers on top of each other and mostly white cells, try a more refined call, like only specifying 1 site and 1 community.

Plot motile invertebrate measurements for all species in Outer Brewster from 2013 to 2019 

outbre <- plotMotileInvertMeas(site = "OUTBRE", years = 2013:2021)
outbre

Plot motile invertebrate measurements for all species in Little Hunter Barnacle photoplots 

barn <- plotMotileInvertMeas(site = "LITHUN", community = "Barnacle")
barn

Plot Littorina species measurements in Little Hunter and add plot title. 

peri <- c("LITLIT", "LITOBT", "LITSAX")
lh_peri2 <- plotMotileInvertMeas(site = "LITHUN", species = peri,
             plot_title = "Littorina spp. (periwinkles)")
lh_peri2

plotPhotoCover()

Plots the photoplot cover summarized as median cover and middle 50% distribution of cover across the photoplots within a target species. Note that there are a lot of arguments that produce different plots and figures (all explained in the help). Here are a few I tend to use the most.

Plot photo cover for all barnacle plots in ACAD 

cov_barn <- plotPhotoCover(park = "ACAD", community = "Barnacle")
cov_barn

Plot only main species groups in Little Hunter 

cov_lh <- plotPhotoCover(site = "LITHUN", main_groups = T) 
cov_lh

Plot only the top 3 highest cover species per community type in Little Hunter 

cov_lh3 <- plotPhotoCover(site = "LITHUN", top_spp = 3)
cov_lh3

Plot cover as heatmap for main groups in Outer Brewster 

out_heat <- plotPhotoCover(site = "OUTBRE", main_groups = T, heatmap = T, plot_title = "Outer Brewster")
out_heat

Plot cover for Fucus community main groups in Calf Island 

calf <- plotPhotoCover(site = "CALISL", main_groups = T, community = "Fucus", plot_title = "Calf Island Fucus community")
calf

plotPISpecies()

This function plots species by bolt elevation a given park, site, and years. The point for each species is the median elevation across the three transects for that year. The ribbon represents upper 75% and lower 25% elevation recorded for a species within a given year. The thicker lines on the error bars are the 25% and 75% quantiles of elevation across the transects. The thinner error bars that end with vertical lines are the minimum and maximum elevation detected along the three transects.

Plot main groups for Bass Harbor and facet by species 

pi_bh <- plotPISpecies(site = "BASHAR", facet = T, main_groups = T)
pi_bh

Plot main groups in Green Island for 2021: 2024 

pi_gi <- plotPISpecies(site = "GREISL", facet = T, main_groups = F, years = 2021:2024)
pi_gi

Plot main groups in Ship Harbor with reversed axis 

shp_main <- plotPISpecies(site = "SHIHAR", rev_axis = T, facet = F, main_groups = T)
shp_main

Plot all species on Transect 1 in Otter Point without faceting on species and custom title. May be helpful for QC. 

op_t1 <- plotPISpecies(site = "OTTPOI", plotName = "T1") + labs(title = "Otter Point: T1")
op_t1

Plot Fucus and Fucus epibiont in Otter Point without faceting on species and dropping y label (b/c axes flipped, this is the xlab). Placing legend at the bottom 

op_fucus <- 
plotPISpecies(site = "OTTPOI", species = c("FUCEPI", "FUCSPP"), xlab = NULL) + 
  labs(title = "Otter Point") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
op_fucus

plotPITransects()

This function plots bolt distance and elevation data by transect for each park, site, and year.

Plot Ship Harbor transect contours for each transect 

trans_shp <- plotPITransects(site = "SHIHAR", years = 2021:2024)
trans_shp

Plot multiple sites in ACAD and fixing the axis scales for context across sites. 

trans3 <- plotPITransects(site = c("BASHAR", "OTTPOI", "SHIHAR"), years = 2021:2024, facet_scales = "fixed")
trans3

Plot BOHA and fixing the axis scales for context across sites for all years and add dashed line at MLLW = 0. 

boha_pi <- plotPITransects(park = "BOHA", facet_scales = "fixed") + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed")
boha_pi

plotSpeciesContours()

This function plots a loess smoothed contour averaging the transects across all years specified. Point intercept minimum and maximum elevation ranges are plotted along the contours by year for each of the main species groups: REDGRP, ASCNOD, FUCSPP, MUSSPP, BARSPP, NONCOR. Photoplot cover is plotted as median cover and median elevation for each target species plot.

Plot Little Hunter all years. 

lh_spp <- plotSpeciesContours(site = "LITHUN")
lh_spp

Plot Bass Harbor every 3 years since monitoring began. 

bh_spp <- plotSpeciesContours(site = "BASHAR", years = seq(2013, as.numeric(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")), 3))
bh_spp

Plot Green Island for 2024. 

gr_pi <- plotSpeciesContours(site = "GREISL", years = 2024)
gr_pi

Plot Green Island for 2024 without photo plot pies. 

gr_pi2 <- plotSpeciesContours(site = "GREISL", years = 2024, include_photoplots = F)
gr_pi2

plotWaterTemp()

This function plots water temperature at high tide by site. Note that function works on compiled logger data, rather than working off the raw logger data. Compiled datasets should be imported using importWaterTemp(). To speed up plotting of multiple sites or long time-series, plot the simplified water temperature data derived from importWaterTemp(simplify = TRUE). Note the data and functions have not been checked recently. Functions in this section not currently active, and were not run for this website.

Plot logger water temp for 2020:2022 in ACAD sites in 1 facet column. 

plotWaterTemp(park = "ACAD", years = 2020:2022, facet_col = 1)

Plot water temp in Bass Harbor for 2011:2022. 

plotWaterTemp(site = "BASHAR", years = 2011:2022)

theme_rocky()

This function customizes a theme for plotting data in the package, including removing the default panel grids from ggplot2 figures.

dat <- sumPhotoCover(site = "SHIHAR", community = "Ascophyllum", species = "ASCNOD")

library(ggplot2)
p <- 
ggplot(dat, aes(x = Year, y = median_cover)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_rocky()

p
